ledger.title: Extragradient on ratio games: last-iterate convergence for 2x2 games with an interior equilibrium
ledger.note: For 2x2 ratio games the gradient descent-ascent field is D^-2 J grad H with separable H=A(p)+B(q) (cubic A, B from the pencil (N,D)); every interior equilibrium is a centre; all closed orbits are convex (normalisation to P g(xi)+R g(zeta), g=t^2/2-t^3/3, and the identity xi^2(3-2zeta)(1-2zeta)-(1-zeta)^2(4xi^2-1)=(1-zeta)^2-xi^2 with smoothstep symmetry); hence H is a Lyapunov function for the exact extragradient map and EG with small constant step converges linearly from every compact sub-level set of the closed-orbit region. Boundary equilibria, starts outside that region and games larger than 2x2 remain open. No prior treatment found in a bounded search.

title: Is PRM=2 for the thesis’s bipartite trading-network model? A platform adds missi…
text: Is PRM=2 for the thesis’s bipartite trading-network model? A platform adds missing buyer–seller edges; unit-demand buyers and unit-supply sellers trade at seller-optimal competitive prices, with platform-favorable tie-breaking. title: For m≥4 alternatives and arbitrary finite electorates with strict rankings, is 3…
text: For m≥4 alternatives and arbitrary finite electorates with strict rankings, is 3/m the largest uniform lower bound alpha such that a randomized social decision scheme satisfying SD-participation can assign probability at least alpha to every Condorcet winner? SD-participation means that, according to each voter’s ranking, the lottery when voting weakly stochastically dominates the lottery after that voter abstains. A Condorcet winner defeats every other alternative by strict pairwise majority. Choosing a uniformly random triple and applying maximin attains 3/m; the question is whether any scheme can attain alpha>3/m uniformly over all profiles.
location: §4.1, p. 39 (PDF p. 53); conclusion, p. 45. Status evidence, checked 5 October 2026: The 2025 thesis explicitly leaves the bound open. Searches combining Romen, participation, approximate Condorcet consistency and 3/m found no later resolution. The author’s earlier joint paper concerns strategyproofness (a stronger axiom), so its 2/m theorem does not settle this participation problem.

title: For finite project sets and arbitrary finite sets of donors with nonempty approv…
text: For finite project sets and arbitrary finite sets of donors with nonempty approval sets A_i and positive endowments C_i, does there exist a distribution rule f assigning the pooled budget among projects that simultaneously satisfies Pareto efficiency, approval monotonicity and contribution incentive-compatibility? Utilities are u_i(delta)=sum_(x in A_i)delta_x. Approval monotonicity means that adding x to one donor’s approval set cannot decrease the allocation to x. Contribution incentive-compatibility requires u_i(f(A))≥u_i(f(A_(-i)))+C_i for each donor when at least two participate; the reduced profile omits both i and C_i. The thesis shows pairwise compatibility but leaves this three-way compatibility open.

title: Does every search problem in search-RL have a pseudodeterministic randomized log…
label: Problem 3.5.1
text: Does every search problem in search-RL have a pseudodeterministic randomized logarithmic-space transducer? Here the relation R has polynomially bounded witnesses verifiable with deterministic logarithmic workspace, two-way input access and one-way witness access; membership in search-RL means some randomized log-space transducer finds a valid witness with inverse-polynomial probability on every valid input. Pseudodeterminism asks for a fixed valid witness y_x for each input x that the new transducer outputs with probability at least 2/3, using fresh one-way random bits and without storing an auxiliary reproducibility seed.

title: One explicitly proposed formulation of the thesis’s #SAT lifting conjecture is t…
label: Conjecture 1
text: One explicitly proposed formulation of the thesis’s #SAT lifting conjecture is the following. Let C be a Boolean circuit class closed under unbounded conjunction and negation. If, for some epsilon>0, the exact number of satisfying assignments of any n-input C-circuit of size at most 2^(n^epsilon) can be computed deterministically in O(2^(n−n^epsilon)) time, must Quasi-NP contain a language with no polynomial-size SYM∘C circuits? Quasi-NP is the union of nondeterministic n^((log n)^k) time classes over constants k; SYM∘C has an arbitrary symmetric Boolean top gate applied to C-subcircuits. This is the Theorem 4.2 version explicitly requested by Conjecture 1; the source labels the overall conjecture informal.

results.label: B3C-01: Weighted interval ULC through nine variables
results.scope: For every integer 0<=m<=9, every binary family on m positions defined by arbitrary integer lower/upper bounds on sums over linear intervals, and all nonnegative real position weights, its weighted rank sequence is ultra-log-concave of order m. Limits: All dimensions and cycle domination remain open; numerical ULC is not coefficientwise ULC.

results.label: B3C-02: All-dimensional endpoint inequalities
results.scope: For every such linear interval family in every integer dimension m>=0 and every nonnegative weight vector, k(m-k)f_k^2 >= (k+1)(m-k+1)f_(k-1)f_(k+1) at k in {1,2,3,4,m-4,m-3,m-2,m-1} intersect {1,...,m-1}. Limits: Middle inequalities in dimensions >=10 are not established. Uses Kahn-Neiman Theorem 9.

results.label: B3C-03: Laminar interval ULC
results.scope: For every integer m>=0, every laminar family of integer-bounded linear intervals on m binary positions, and all nonnegative position weights, the weighted feasible-word ranks are ULC of order m. Limits: Typical overlapping path neighborhoods are not laminar. Convolution closure is published, not claimed new.

results.label: B3C-10: One-bit inclusion matching fails
results.scope: In dimension six, equations x1+x2=x2+x3=x4+x5=x5+x6=1 give rank counts (0,0,1,2,1,0,0). The unique rank-two word 010010 has no feasible rank-three superset. Limits: Refutes the stated stronger matching route, not APP or ULC. The stalled agent matching definition was not supplied.

results.label: B3C-11: Coefficientwise ULC fails
results.scope: The unrestricted two-variable family has central normalized ULC defect w1^2-2*w1*w2+w2^2, whose mixed coefficient is -2. Limits: Numerical nonnegativity survives, since the defect is (w1-w2)^2.

text: For a finite Weyl group W, let U be the interval [e,u] in right weak order and define W/U = {w: ℓ(wx) = ℓ(w)+ℓ(x) for every x in U}, where ℓ is Coxeter length. Is multiplication from (W/U) × U to W bijective exactly when u is separable? Separability is recursive: rank-one elements qualify; reducible systems qualify componentwise; otherwise some simple root α has all positive roots containing α either inverted by u or all uninverted, and the restriction obtained by deleting α is separable. Restriction intersects the inversion set with the parabolic root subsystem.

title: If X is a finite 3-connected planar graph, must its quantum automorphism group Q…
text: If X is a finite 3-connected planar graph, must its quantum automorphism group Qut(X) be a closed quantum subgroup of the free orthogonal quantum group O₃⁺? The algebra C(Qut(X)) is generated by a magic unitary commuting with the adjacency matrix: a matrix of projections whose rows and columns sum to 1. title: How fast do the following dynamics reach R-polarization? There are m user vector…
text: How fast do the following dynamics reach R-polarization? There are m user vectors u_j and n creator vectors v_i on the unit sphere in R^d. Each round recommends i_j to user j with probabilities p_ij ≥ p₀ > 0. Write P(x)=x/‖x‖₂ and J_i={j:i_j=i}. Simultaneously update u_j to P(u_j+ηᵤ f(v_iⱼ,u_j)v_iⱼ) and v_i to P(v_i+(η_c/|J_i|)Σ_{j∈J_i}sign(⟨u_j,v_i⟩)u_j); unchosen creators stay fixed. Assume f has the sign of its inner product, L_f ≤ |f| ≤ 1 off zero, and 0 < η_c ≤ ηᵤL_f/2, ηᵤ < 1/2. R-polarization means that every vector lies within Euclidean distance R of c or −c for some unit c. Determine quantitative bounds on the time to this event from almost every initial state, including dependence on the initial configuration and model parameters.

Origin: Joint definability questions with Søren Brinck Knudstorp; collaboration credited in the thesis and March 2025 preprint.

Shared setup for questions 240, 241, 242: Teams are subsets $t\subseteq2^X$, with fixed finite $X$. Atoms hold at every valuation; conjunction requires both conjuncts; $\bot$ holds only at $\varnothing$. Define $t\models\varphi\to\psi$ iff every $s\subseteq t$ supporting $\varphi$ supports $\psi$, and $t\models\Diamond\varphi$ iff some nonempty $s\subseteq t$ supports $\varphi$. Let $D(\varphi,\psi)$ mean $\exists s,u\,[t\subseteq s\cup u,\ s\models\varphi,\ u\models\psi]$, and $G(\varphi,\psi)$ mean $\exists s\supseteq t\,[s\models\varphi\text{ or }s\models\psi]$. Language A uses atoms, $\bot,\land,\to,\Diamond$; B adds G; C uses atoms, $\bot,\land,D,\Diamond$, functional-dependence atoms, and negated classical formulas. A dependence atom requires valuations agreeing on its input variables to agree on its output variable. Classical formulas use atoms, $\bot,\land,D$ and classical negation only. Uniform definability requires one formula context for every eligible argument pair.

results.label: 2026-10-09: proposed full proof
results.scope: The independent-edge, bidirectional-vertical bunkbed inequality holds for every transitive tournament. The proof allows any common horizontal retention probability and independent vertex-dependent vertical probabilities; at probability one half the gap for u<v is at least 2^(-(v-u+2)). Write $a_k=\operatorname{lct}((X^{N_k})_{\rm ss},\Delta_{N_k};D_k)$ and $b_k=\operatorname{lct}(X^{N_k},\Delta_{N_k};D_k)$, using the diagonal $G$-semistable locus for $L^{\boxtimes N_k}$. Here $\operatorname{lct}(Y,B;D)$ is the supremum of $c$ for which $|s_D|^{-2c}|s_B|^{-2}$ is locally integrable; smooth choices of norms do not change it. Set $\gamma_{\rm PS}=\liminf_k a_k$ and $\gamma=\liminf_k b_k$.

title: Find sound and complete axiomatizations of the full, arbitrarily nested $K$-only…
label: Problem 2.1
text:
Find sound and complete axiomatizations of the full, arbitrarily nested $K$-only language for H-, N-, and S-semantics. A model has nonempty $W$, serial $D$, and a well-founded preorder $\le_w$ on $W_w\subseteq W$ with $w\le_w v$ for every $v\in W_w$. Let $B\varphi$ mean truth at all $D$-successors, and $A\Rightarrow_w C$ mean truth of $C$ at all $\le_w$-minimal $A$-worlds in $W_w$. Then $K_H\varphi:=B\varphi\land(
eg\varphi\Rightarrow_w
eg B\varphi)$; $K_N\varphi:=B\varphi\land(
eg\varphi\Rightarrow_w
eg B\varphi)\land(\varphi\Rightarrow_w B\varphi)$; and $K_S\varphi:=B\varphi\land(B\varphi\Rightarrow_w\varphi)$. Here $B$ and $\Rightarrow$ are semantic notation, not target-language connectives.

title: Are all trigram languages and all precedence languages in the range of Heinz’s F…
text: Are all trigram languages and all precedence languages in the range of Heinz’s Forward Backward Neighborhood Learner? Specifically, does every such L have a finite positive sample S⊆L for which the learner outputs an acceptor for exactly L? The learner merges equal (1,1)-neighborhood states to a fixed point separately in the sample’s prefix and suffix trees, then intersects their accepted languages. Trigram languages constrain boundary-marked contiguous blocks of length three; precedence languages prohibit specified ordered symbol pairs as possibly noncontiguous subsequences.

title: Let $R$ be real closed, $K=R(i)$, $G=\mathbb G_a\times\mathbb G_m$, and $n>1$. L…
text: Let $R$ be real closed, $K=R(i)$, $G=\mathbb G_a\times\mathbb G_m$, and $n>1$. Let $V\subseteq G^n$ be absolutely irreducible and perfectly rotund: $\dim V=n$, every nonzero integer linear combination of additive coordinates and monomial in multiplicative coordinates is nonconstant, and $\dim(A\cdot V)>\operatorname{rank}A$ when $0<\operatorname{rank}A<n$. Define $r(z,w)=((\operatorname{Re}z,|w|),(i\operatorname{Im}z,w/|w|))$ coordinatewise, grouping the real and imaginary blocks, and let $\check V=\overline{r(V)}^{\rm Zar}$. If $M=(N\mid Q)$ with $N,Q\in\operatorname{Mat}_n(\mathbb Z)$ invertible over $\mathbb Q$ satisfies $\dim(M\cdot\check V)=n$, is $v\mapsto M\cdot r(v)$ surjective from $V(K)$ onto $(M\cdot\check V)(K)$? Matrices act linearly on additive coordinates and by monomials on multiplicative coordinates.

title: Let $V$ be finite and $U=\{(A,B):A\cup B=V\}$, ordered by $(A,B)\le(C,D)$ iff $A…
label: Problem 3.2.5
text: Let $V$ be finite and $U=\{(A,B):A\cup B=V\}$, ordered by $(A,B)\le(C,D)$ iff $A\subseteq C$ and $B\supseteq D$. Set $(A,B)^*=(B,A)$, $(A,B)\vee(C,D)=(A\cup C,B\cap D)$, and $(A,B)\wedge(C,D)=(A\cap C,B\cup D)$. Let $f:U\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}$ satisfy $f(s)=f(s^*)$ and $f(r\vee s)+f(r\wedge s)\le f(r)+f(s)$, and let $S_k=\{s:f(s)<k\}$. A $k$-profile chooses one orientation of each separation in $S_k$, is downward closed there, and has $(r\vee s)^*\notin\tau$ whenever $r,s\in\tau$; it is regular if no $(V,A)$ belongs to it. For $k\in\mathbb N$, if a $k$-profile $\tau'$ extends to a regular $2k$-profile, must some $X\subseteq V$ satisfy $|A\cap X|<|B\cap X|$ for every $(A,B)\in\tau'$?

title: Consider N unit-speed servers with processor sharing: a server divides its capac…
label: Conjecture 4.2
text: Consider N unit-speed servers with processor sharing: a server divides its capacity equally among its unfinished replicas. Jobs arrive as a Poisson process of rate λ. Each job independently chooses d distinct servers uniformly, 1 ≤ d ≤ N, and places one replica at each. Its service requirements (X₁,…,X_d) have an arbitrary fixed joint distribution, with identical nonnegative marginals X satisfying 0 < E[X] < ∞; vectors are independent across jobs and independent of arrivals and assignments. Replicas are cancelled immediately when the first finishes. Does λ d E[min(X₁,…,X_d)] < N imply stability of the stochastic system, i.e. positive recurrence of the full queueing state process (including service requirements or attained service), rather than merely stability of its fluid model? For nonexchangeable replica laws, assign replica labels uniformly to the selected servers.
location: Conjecture 4.2, §4.3.6, printed p. 81; model §4.2 p. 65; fluid-limit/stochastic distinction pp. 64–65 and 80–81.

title: Use Tse’s fixed-block variable-length quantization model (§§2.1, 3.1): the obser…
label: Conjecture 3.5.3
text: Use Tse’s fixed-block variable-length quantization model (§§2.1, 3.1): the observed source state $H_n\in\{0,1\}$ flips with probability $\alpha$, and samples are conditionally independent with state-dependent distributions. Quantizers depend on source and buffer states; the buffer has capacity $L$ and drains $R_c$ bits/slot. Let $D_i(R)$ be the convexified operational distortion-rate functions, with $D_0'(R_c)<D_1'(R_c)$. Define $V^*(c)$ by the fluid problem in §3.5: the source flips at rate one, the buffer $y\in[0,c]$ follows controlled drifts $\mu_i(y)$ preserving this interval, and running cost is $D_i(R_c+\mu_i(y))$. Is it true that, for every $\varepsilon>0$ and $L\to\infty$, $\alpha L\to c>0$, ergodic buffer-control schemes attain $\limsup D_q(L,\alpha)\le V^*(c)+\varepsilon$ while $p_f(L,\alpha)$ decays exponentially in $L$? Here $V^*$ is the minimum long-run average fluid cost, $D_q$ the stationary distortion contribution from nonfull-buffer slots, and $p_f$ the stationary full-buffer probability.

title: What is the noisy-permutation capacity of the following $q$-symbol “zigzag” chan…
text: What is the noisy-permutation capacity of the following $q$-symbol “zigzag” channel, for $q\ge3$? Its transition matrix satisfies $W_{i,i}=a_i$, $W_{i,i+1}=1-a_i$ for $i<q$, $0<a_i<1$, and $W_{q,q}=1$, with all other entries zero. A length-$n$ input passes independently through $W$ and its outputs are then uniformly permuted. Capacity is the supremum of achievable rates $\liminf_{n\to\infty}\log M_n/\log n$ over codes whose average decoding error tends to zero.

title: Sharp intermediate budgets for weighted decision-data compression
label: Conjecture 6.5
text: For finite $D\subset\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^m$, let $L_D(W)=|D|^{-1}\sum_{(x,y)\in D}\|Wx-y\|_2^2$ and $L_D^*=\min_W L_D(W)>0$. Let $A^*$ return the minimum-Frobenius-norm weighted least-squares minimizer. Define $F_w(d,m,n)=\sup_D\inf_{S\subset D,\,|S|\le n,\,w\in\Delta(S)}L_D(A^*(\sum_{z\in S}w_z\ell_z))/L_D^*$. Determine the remaining intermediate profile, especially $d<n<(m+1)d-1$ for $m\ge2$, excluding resolved endpoint and low-dimensional cells. The smallest reported vector conjectures are $F_w(2,2,3)=13/8$ and $F_w(2,2,4)=5/4$; these form one profile question.

Can expected regret against the best intervention be poly(n)√T polylog(T), without a positive lower bound on nonzero coefficients? title: Iterated-logarithm stopping boundaries for nonparametric best-arm GLRs
text:
For K independently sampled arms with laws on known [0,B], let $\widehat
u_{t,a}$ and $N_{t,a}$ be empirical laws and adaptive counts; m denotes a law’s mean. Define $Z_t(i)=\inf_{\kappa\in\mathcal P([0,B])^K:\,\exists j
e i,\,m(\kappa_j)\ge m(\kappa_i)}\sum_aN_{t,a}D_{m KL}(\widehat
u_{t,a}\|\kappa_a)$. Stop when $\max_iZ_t(i)>c(t,\delta)$, recommending a maximizer. Under every adaptive sampling rule, can wrong-stopping probability be ≤δ with $c(t,\delta)=O(\log\log t)$ for fixed δ and $\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}c(t,\delta)/\log(1/\delta)=1$ for fixed t? This is the empirical-law GLR, not a generic confidence interval.

title: Is decoder-only side information enough for the conditional-dependence exponent?

Is the optimal type-II Stein exponent E(R) equal to the exponent Ẽ(R) when the encoder also receives Z^n? The latter is max_{P_{U|XZ}:I_P(U;X|Z)≤R} min_{P̃:P̃_UXZ=P_UXZ, P̃_UYZ=P_UYZ} D(P̃_UXYZ || P_{U|XZ}Q_XYZ), with |U|≤|X||Z|+1. General equality is open; Z=g(X) is already solved. title: Finite-time regret of likelihood-projection sampling over latent orders
text: There are k arms with independent Gaussian rewards N(μ_a,σ²), known σ, and a known finite collection of m order-constrained mean sets H_s; the unknown μ belongs to their union. Put M_a={v:v_a≥v_b for all b} and Σ_a=∪_{s:a maximal in s} H_s. At each round, lobTS assigns arm a probability proportional to exp(−d_a(t)/(2σ²)), where d_a(t)=inf_{v∈M_a∩Σ_a}∑_b N_b(t)(v_b−μ̂_b(t))² (empty set gives zero probability). It starts with no observations; unobserved coordinates have zero weight. What finite-time frequentist bound holds for R_T=E∑_{t≤T}(max_b μ_b−μ_{A_t}), as a function of T, the gaps and order structure? In particular, is R_T=o(T) for every well-specified instance with a unique best arm? This asks about the specified heuristic, not existence of some low-regret algorithm.
location: Current v2 (18 August 2026), §3.2, Algorithm 2 and printed pp. 6–7.

title: Remove the dimension loss in variation-adaptive two-point dynamic regret
text: Let X⊂R^d be compact convex with rB₂⊂X⊂RB₂. An oblivious sequence of convex G-Lipschitz, L-smooth losses f_t is observed only through two exact function values per round. The loss charged is their average. For an oblivious comparator sequence u_t, define P_T=∑_{t=2}^T||u_t−u_{t−1}||₂ and V_T=∑_{t=2}^T sup_{x∈X}||∇f_t(x)−∇f_{t−1}(x)||₂². Can the extra factor d in the source’s expected dynamic-regret guarantee Õ(√[d³(1+P_T+V_T)(1+P_T)]) be removed, while retaining its P_T,V_T dependence and not knowing P_T? The target is the √d rather than d^{3/2} leading dimension dependence; determine if it is attainable or intrinsically impossible, preserving initialization/lower-order terms where needed.

title: Does time-dependent Pandora search admit a PTAS?
text: In Pandora’s Box Over Time there are n boxes, integer processing delays p_i≥0, and an explicit horizon H≥n+∑_i p_i. Inspecting unused box i at time t costs c_i(t)≥0, draws V_it from a known nonnegative distribution D_it, and prevents another inspection before t+1+p_i. All box-time draws are independent. Stopping is allowed only after every initiated inspection has completed (t_i+p_i≤T). At stopping time T≤H, collect max_{inspected i} v̄_i(V_it,T−t−p_i), minus all inspection costs; 0≤v̄_i(v,τ)≤v̄_i(v,0)=v. Waiting and adaptive inspection/stopping are allowed. Does this optimization problem admit a polynomial-time approximation scheme, or can one rule out a PTAS under a standard complexity assumption? Preserve the source’s value-oracle access for expected maxima of reservation-truncated independent rewards, or state an explicit finite-support encoding. Approximation is multiplicative relative to optimal expected net utility, with stopping without inspection available.
location: §2 model and §2.1 oracle model; §5 conclusions, printed p. 17.

title: Efficient optimal stopping under a finite mixture of product distributions
text: There are m known scenarios, each specifying n distributions on a common set of k reward values. A scenario is sampled uniformly once; conditional on it, the n rewards are sampled independently. Rewards arrive in their fixed order. A policy observes the prefix and must irrevocably stop on one observed current reward, maximizing expected payoff. Can an optimal online stopping policy be computed in time polynomial in m,n,k (and the bit length for rational inputs)? If exact optimization is intractable, what approximation to the optimal online payoff is possible? The computational output must permit the policy’s stop/continue decision at an observed history without expanding an exponential history tree.
subject: Optimization & Operations Research

title: Half-prophet utility under an unobserved additive common cause
text: Let Z,X_1,…,X_n be mutually independent nonnegative random variables with known bounded-support laws. Only Y_i=Z+X_i is revealed, sequentially in fixed order; neither Z nor any X_i is directly observed. Does every such instance admit a possibly randomized stopping rule τ∈{1,…,n}, adapted to the revealed Y-prefixes, satisfying E[Y_τ]≥(1/2)E[max_iY_i]? The rule may use the whole observation history and must accept a current value irrevocably, taking the last value if necessary. It is not restricted to one fixed threshold.

title: Remove the dimension penalty from one-batch trajectory-preference exploration
text: Consider the source's discounted MDP with known continuous features φ(s,a)∈R^d, ||φ(s,a)||≤L, unknown linear reward rθ*(s,a)=〈θ*,φ(s,a)〉, ||θ*||≤B, and trajectory features Φ(τ)=∑h≥0 γ^hφ(sh,ah). Independent comparison labels satisfy P(τ≻τ′)=σ(〈θ*,Φ(τ)−Φ(τ′)〉). A learner can execute policies and call a polynomial-time (ε,δ)-PAC reward-optimization oracle for any proposed reward vector. Can computationally tractable preference-free exploration, collecting T trajectory pairs before a single final batch of labels, remove the extra √d from the high-probability final policy loss bound Õ(√(κd³/T)), achieving Õ(√(κd²/T)) under the same access assumptions? Here κ=max|z|≤2BL/(1−γ) 1/σ′(z), and loss is V*θ*−Vπ̂θ*.

title: Find a weighted minimum cut from ordinal cut comparisons efficiently
text: An unknown undirected graph on a known vertex set V, |V|=n has nonnegative edge weights. Write c(S)=∑{u,v}:u∈S,v∉S wuv for each nonempty proper S⊂V. The only weight access is an exact oracle returning sign(c(S)−c(T)) for two such cuts. In the source’s oracle model (two n-bit cut indicators per query, a unit-cost oracle call), is there an algorithm using polynomially many queries and polynomial additional computation that returns an exact global minimum cut for arbitrary nonnegative weights? The source leaves the weighted extension open even for integer weights in [0,B]; distinguish polynomial dependence on the bit length log B from the known (nB)^{O(r² log B)} special-case bound for r distinct weighted degrees. No comparisons of differences of cut values or arbitrary edge subsets are available.

text: Let n≥3, δ<1/(6n²), and unknown distinct values vi∈(0,1]∩δZ define x*v(p)∈argmax{vᵀx:x∈[0,1]^n,pᵀx≤B}, with an unknown fixed greedy tie-breaking order. Prices p range only over [0,1]^n. The known capacity satisfies B≤(n−1)(min vi/max vi−δ²/n²). An oracle returns sign(wᵀx*v(p)−wᵀx*v(q)) for any two prices, with fixed unknown w∈R^n_{>0}. Determine the sharp worst-case comparison complexity of recovering v up to positive scale with success probability at least 2/3 over all admissible instances. In particular, is the additive B² overhead in O(n log(1/δ)+B²) necessary, or can recovery uniformly match the Ω(n log(1/δ)) lower bound? The unresolved gap matters when B² dominates n log(1/δ).

title: Achieve square-root accuracy from sigmoid comparisons of bundles

After T calls output Ŝ and measure expected simple regret E[f(Ŝ)−minS f(S)]. Can a computationally efficient algorithm attain T^(−1/2) decay, with polynomial dependence on n for each fixed b, rather than the source’s O_b(n^(7/5)T^(−2/5)) bound? Establish the sharp rate. The source conjectures the square-root T exponent; its general lower bound is Ω_b(n/√T), while Ω_b(n^(3/2)/√T) is proved only when every queried pair differs in O(1) elements.

title: When can one mediator implement a learning equilibrium?
text: Characterize two-player games with convex polytope action sets X,Y and bilinear utilities for which every profile correlated equilibrium is the projection of a correlated equilibrium of the vertex normal-form game. A correlated profile is φ∈conv{x⊗y}. It is a profile CE when, separately for each player, φ admits a convex decomposition into product profiles where that player is best responding; the decompositions may differ. title: Uniform equilibrium in finite multiplayer stochastic games
label: Problem 1
text: Does every stochastic game with finitely many players, states and actions, perfect monitoring and bounded stage payoffs admit a uniform equilibrium payoff? At interior t0 assume F0 has continuous positive density f0(t0), and the inspection density h(t,u) extends continuously to the diagonal near(t0,t0) with h(t0,t0)>0 and 0<F0(t0)<1. Determine the correct pointwise normalization and nondegenerate limiting law of the unrestricted MLE F̂_n(t0)−F0(t0) when inspection intervals can be arbitrarily short. The familiar proposed (n log n)^(1/3) Chernoff law is not assumed.

title: Universality with arbitrary stationary-ergodic side information

With W_n(b)=∏_t〈b_t,x_t〉, can a causal strategy achieve E[sup_{g∈G,θ1:S∈Δ_m}log(W_n((θ_{g(Z_t)})_t)/W_n(b))]=o(n) for every stationary ergodic Z process, without the extra Eρ_{G×G}(Z^n)=o(n/log²n) condition? Here ρ_H= sup_{h∈H}|Σ_t(h(Z_t)−Eh(Z_t))| and H={1{g≠g′}:g,g′∈G}. Returns may depend on Z; they need not be stationary.

title: Do betting audits require a wider interval than frequency audits?
text: Does there exist a binary path ω with I_CH(ω) strictly contained in I_C(ω)? Here I_R(ω) is the intersection of all closed probability intervals I⊆[0,1] for which ω is R-random; CH denotes Church randomness and C computable randomness. The CH intersection is attained, while C is interpreted through almost randomness: randomness for every strict enlargement [inf I−ε₁,sup I+ε₂]∩[0,1]. title: Efficient dependent-data prediction without observing update sites
text: Let X_t∈{0,1}^n follow unknown Ising Glauber dynamics: choose I_t uniformly from[n], resample coordinate I_t as Bernoulli(σ(Σ_{j≠I_t}A_{I_tj}X_{t−1,j}+h_{I_t})), and leave all other coordinates fixed, where σ is logistic, A is symmetric with zero diagonal, and every free coefficient is in[−B,B], B≥1. X_0 is known. Can an algorithm observing X_t but not I_t, with an agnostic ERM oracle for any binary VC-d class F, run in poly(n,T,B) time and retain EReg_T(F)≲√(dT)(1+n²√log(BTn))? Labels are Y_t=f*(X_t) for an arbitrary fixed f*, possibly outside F, and are revealed after prediction.

ledger.note: Answer no: a positive fixed symmetric (circular) copula with harmonic weights gives an almost-surely singular weak limit (R3). title: Sharp quantile-decision complexity under one-bit feedback
text: With K i.i.d. arms, a pull returns only 1{Xₖ≤θ}; the reporting sensor has no reward memory. Let Qₖ(p)=inf{x: Fₖ(x)≥p}, Qₖ⁺(p)=sup{x: Fₖ(x)≤p}, q∈(0, 1), Qₖ(q)∈[0,λ], 0<ε≤λ, and Aε={k: Qₖ(q)≥maxₐQₐ(q)−ε}. Fix c≥1 and ε̃=λ/ceil((c+1)λ/ε). For k∉Aε set Δₖ=sup{z∈[0, min(q, 1−q)]: Qₖ(q+z)≤maxₐQₐ⁺(q−z)−ε̃}; for k∈Aε set Δₖ=max_{Aε⊆S⊆[K]}sup{z∈[0, minₐ∉SΔₐ]: Qₖ⁺(q−z)≥maxₐ∈S\{k}Qₐ(q+z)−cε̃}, with empty minimum/maximum +∞/−∞. Put dₖ=max(Δₖ, maxₐ∈AεΔₐ)>0. Can the log(1/dₖ) factor in O(Σₖdₖ⁻²[log(1/δ)+log(1/dₖ)+log(cλK/ε)]) become log log(1/dₖ), and what is the sharp joint gap/range dependence? results.label: B3C-07: Degree-dependent s-Eulerian representation bound
results.scope: Every nonconstant s-Eulerian polynomial of integer degree d>=1 has a representing positive integer vector of length at most 2d-1. Limits: Existential bound after deleting units and contracting all-two blocks; all-degree sharpness for (1+ux)^d is not recovered.

results.label: B3C-08: Connected quadratic s-Eulerian inequality
results.scope: For every positive integer vector s with all entries >=2, if E_s(x)=1+h_1 x+h_2 x^2 has degree exactly two, then h_1>h_2>0. Limits: Degree-two blocks only; does not establish simple roots for every nonunit block. Exceptional (2,6,3) coefficients corrected to (1,19,16).

results.label: B3C-09: Exact uncoloured multiplicity (2,b) classification
results.scope: For every positive integer b, A_(2,b)(x)=1+2b x+binom(b,2)x^2 is s-Eulerian for some positive integer vector of arbitrary length iff b=2 or b(b+1)/2 is an integer square. Limits: Exact subfamily of general coloured multiset question Q1262; not full classification.

ledger.title: Collection question 1262: Which colored multiset polynomials are s-Eulerian?
ledger.note: Finite recognition for arbitrary allowed vector length: enumerate ordered factorizations of N=p(1) with optional unit separators; length at most 2*Omega(N)-1 suffices. Complete exclusion for multiplicities (2,3). Infinite Pell family: A_(2,b)=E_(b-t+1,1,b+t+1) whenever b(b+1)/2=t^2. Exactly decided 28 bounded-volume uncolored two-symbol cases. Remaining: A general structural classification of colored multiplicity pairs remains unresolved. The source already uses unit-removal and volume factorization in Proposition 25. B3 continuation (7 Oct): B3C-07 Degree-dependent s-Eulerian representation bound; B3C-08 Connected quadratic s-Eulerian inequality; B3C-09 Exact uncoloured multiplicity (2,b) classification; none closes the question. Recorded from the external B3 return  (backfilled 2026-10-08); initial argument review and bounded independent controls in the intake; not independently re-derived here.

results.label: B3C-05: Uniform interpolation disk through degree five
results.scope: For every integer 1<=n<=5 and every real parameter tuple (a_1,...,a_n) in [0,1]^n, all zeros of P(z)=sum_(j=0)^n e_(n-j)(a) binom(z,j) satisfy |z+1/2|<=n-1/2. Boundary zeros occur only at the all-zero and all-one parameter polynomials. Thus R_n=n for 1<=n<=5. Limits: Exact certificate proof uniformly covers parameters, but only degrees through five. Reported degrees six to eight are not recovered.

results.label: B3C-06: All-degree equal-parameter interpolation disk
results.scope: For every integer n>=1 and every real a in [0,1], all zeros of the polynomial with L(P)(u)=(u+a)^n satisfy |z+1/2|<=n-1/2, strictly for 0<a<1. For n>=2, |z+1/2|^2 <= (n-1/2)^2-8a(1-a)(n-1). Limits: One-parameter family; arbitrary independent parameters in higher degrees remain open.

results.label: B3C-12: Arbitrary interpolation shift mixtures violate the disk
results.scope: For n=4, P(z)=binom(z,4)+binom(z+4,4) has a root with |z+1/2|>7/2; 24P(w-1/2)=2w^4+43w^2+105/8. Limits: Outside the TP class: sampled numerator 1+t^4 is not real-rooted. Does not refute Q1442.

Setup for questions 1692, 1693: A radius-r hard-sphere Gibbs law on X is supported on point sets with mutual distances ≥2r. Conditional on points outside each bounded region, points inside follow a rate-λ Poisson process conditioned on mutual separation and separation from outside points. In empty-start birth–death dynamics, proposed points arrive at intensity λ per unit volume and time, are accepted only at distance ≥2r from existing points, and die after independent Exp(1) lifetimes.

Setup for question 1699: Let P be a law on positive integers with finite mean and P(1)<1. results.label: 2026-10-09: proposed counterexample
results.scope: An explicit 13-dimensional two-generated nilpotent Lie algebra of class five has property F for every generating pair over every characteristic-zero field, but is not free nilpotent. Its graded dimensions are 2,1,2,3,5 and its center has dimension five. Limits: Disproves the proposed equivalence. No smallest-dimension or full classification claim is made.

ledger.title: Collection question 1885: Universal BST lower bound
ledger.note: Almost-sure liminf H_n/log n >= c_* if mu has continuous positive density on any nondegenerate rectangle touching the left edge; no condition outside that rectangle. Scope: Arbitrary permuton mu (uniform marginals); sort iid mu-points by x and insert y-values into a BST; graph height and c_*>2 satisfying c_* log(2e/c_*)=1. Restrictions/extensions: For the partial theorem only: restrict mu to a continuous positive density on one nondegenerate left-edge rectangle; outside it mu may be singular. Convergence is strengthened to an almost-sure liminf in the nested iid coupling. Remaining: The universal arbitrary-permuton lower bound, including singular cases, remains. Filed from the external B6 return; scope reading and selected controls do not constitute an independent full proof audit or a formal certificate.

Setup for questions 2079, 2080: Sequences comprise finite structures. FO-convergence means convergence of satisfaction probabilities for every first-order formula under independent uniform vertex sampling. A graph modeling is strong if aν(A)≤bν(B) whenever a,b∈N and measurable A,B have every A-vertex adjacent to at least a B-vertices and every B-vertex to at most b A-vertices.

ledger.title: Collection question 2168: Presburger complexity at Σ4
ledger.note: Yes. For any positive transcendental t, let W=Q[t]+span_Q{(t+n)^-1: n≥1} and P=W×Z, lexicographic with W more significant and 1=(0,1). P has a Σ4 Scott sentence and no Π4 Scott sentence, so SC(P)=Σ4. Scope: Full retained question; written proof (Part I) using Presburger quantifier elimination and Montalbán's orbit theorem. Not independently re-derived.

results.label: 2026-10-09: proposed full proof
results.scope: For every field F and finite-dimensional V, Inn(End_F(V)) consists exactly of restrictions of invertible conjugations to the full domain, the zero-matrix singleton, and D(U,W)={a:im(a) is contained in U, W is contained in ker(a)} with U,W both proper nonzero subspaces. Explicit equality, multiplication and inversion formulas give an isomorphism description. Limits: The zero is the identity on the singleton {0}, not an empty partial map. All dimensions, nonsemisimple products and arbitrary fields are covered; the separate residual-finiteness question Q2304 is not addressed.

Put B⊙B={bc:b,c∈B,b≠c}.

Doctoral context for question 2882: see question 2875.

Origin for question 2882: Explicit journal-paper question.

Setup for question 2882: A finite-word Parikh automaton has letter-reading transitions adding vectors in N^d, and accepts by final state and a semilinear constraint on the total. A resolver selects the next transition from the transition-run prefix ρ and next letter a, and must accept every word in the automaton’s language. It is DPA-implementable if, for each a and transition δ, {ρ:t(ρ,a)=δ} is recognized by a deterministic Parikh automaton over the transition alphabet.

Origin for question 2932: MacManus–Mineh’s CCC question, following work of Gao–Jackson–Seward.

Setup for question 2932: A finite T⊂G is a tile if G=⊔_{d∈D}dT for some D⊂G. A CCC sequence consists of such tilings (D_n,T_n) with 1∈D_n∩T_n, T_n⊆T_{n+1}, ⋃T_n=G, and each partition {dT_n:d∈D_n} refining the next.

source.title: Measured foliations at infinity of quasi-Fuchsian manifolds

context:
Field: Hyperbolic geometry and Teichmüller theory.

Doctoral context for questions 2936, 2937: see question 2928.

Origin for question 2936: Schlenker’s filling question, restated by Choudhury–Marković after the doctoral work.

Origin for question 2937: Schlenker’s questions, restated by Choudhury–Marković after the doctoral work.

Setup for questions 2936, 2937: Fix a closed oriented surface S of genus at least two. For a marked non-Fuchsian quasifuchsian M≅S×R with conformal ends X,Y, set q_+=β_X(Y), q_−=β_Y(X), using the Bers embeddings. Let F_±(M) be the horizontal measured foliations of q_±. A pair fills S if i(F_+,μ)+i(F_−,μ)>0 for every nonzero measured lamination μ.
status_notes: Status for questions 2936, 2937, checked 7 October 2026: The paper proves results near the Fuchsian locus. Later searches found no general resolution.

source.title: Rotated odometers

context:

Primary source: https://doi.org/10.1112/jlms.12731

Doctoral context for questions 2949, 2950: see question 2945.

Origin for questions 2949, 2950: Final journal §1.6, Problems 1.10–1.11; author-manuscript p. 5.

Setup for questions 2949, 2950: On I=[0,1), define a(x)=x−1+3·2^(−n) when 1−2^(1−n)≤x<1−2^(−n), n≥1. Let q≥2, π permute q symbols, Rπ translate the q equal half-open intervals accordingly, and Fπ=a∘Rπ. Form I* by adjoining 1 and splitting each nonzero point in forward or defined backward orbits of D₀={Rπ⁻¹(1−2⁻ⁿ):n≥0} into adjacent x⁻<x⁺, with the order topology and continuous extension Fπ*. Its aperiodic Cantor part is Inp*, with unique minimal subset Imin*. Use the unique invariant probability on Imin*, and normalized transported Lebesgue measure on Inp* when positive.
status_notes: Status for questions 2949, 2950, checked 7 October 2026: The final journal retains both questions. The map formula follows Bruin–Lukina (2025), Eq. (1.1), correcting the earlier printed exponent; no later resolution found.

Setup for questions 3028, 3029, 3030: M is a closed connected oriented smooth 3-manifold. Origin for question 3037: Cárdenas-Andaur’s 2024 paper question, retained in the thesis.

Setup for question 3037: A tied link partitions its components into color classes. The AJ-bracket P(D)∈Z[A^{±1},c] is invariant under Reidemeister II–III, equals 1 on the unknot, and multiplies by c upon adding a new-color split circle, or by −A²−A⁻² for an existing-color circle. Monochromatic crossings obey P(crossing)=A P(A-smoothing)+A⁻¹P(B-smoothing). For a dichromatic crossing, P(crossing)+P(switched)=(A+A⁻¹)(P(A-smoothing)+P(B-smoothing)), merging the two color classes globally in either smoothing. For oriented D, J_t(L)=(-A)^{-3w(D)}P(D).

Setup for questions 3273, 3274, 3275: J⊇Fin is a proper ideal on ω; Eq(f,g)={n:f(n)=g(n)}. A J-MED family E⊆ω^ω has pairwise J-small agreement sets, and every h agrees with some f∈E on a J-positive set. Van Douwen means maximality after restriction to every J-positive X. Finite productivity requires every finite tuple h_i to have f_i∈E with ⋂Eq(h_i,f_i)∉J. The ω-centered version requires every sequence h_i to have f_i∈E and B∉J with B\Eq(h_i,f_i)∈J for all i. A P-point U is a nonprincipal ultrafilter whose countable subfamilies have pseudointersections in U; f≡_U g iff Eq(f,g)∈U.

Setup for question 3372: Let A be countably infinite equality atoms, acted on by all permutations. Input integer linear inequalities Mx≥b have hereditarily orbit-finite row and variable sets and finitely supported coefficients, specified by finite orbit presentations. source.title: On Cospectral Graphons

context:
Field: Combinatorics / graph theory.

Iľkovič: Leipzig doctoral defense 2026; advisors Daniel Kráľ and Richard Montgomery.

Joint-paper question.

Graphons are symmetric measurable [0,1]²→[0,1] functions, using Lebesgue measure. Cospectral means equal t(C_k,W)=∫∏_{i=1}^k W(x_i,x_(i+1))dx_1⋯dx_k for every k≥3, with x_(k+1)=x_1. Cut distance is inf_φ sup_{S,T}|∫_{S×T}(U(φ(x),φ(y))−W(x,y))dxdy|, over measure-preserving bijections φ and measurable S,T. Finite graphs are simple; convergence means cut-distance convergence of their equal-cell adjacency graphons, with orders tending to infinity.

An order tree is rooted with well-ordered predecessor sets. R(T) consists of nonempty downward-closed chains without maxima, as a subspace of {0,1}^T. Ray spaces are homeomorphic to such R(T). context:
Field: Game theory / tournament design.

P∈[0,1]^{n×n} satisfies p_ij+p_ji=1. A tournament is a randomized rule independent of P that sequentially selects matches, won by i against j with conditional probability p_ij, and declares one winner after a bounded number of matches. Write π_i(P) for winning probabilities. Symmetry means π_{σ(i)}(Q)=π_i(P) whenever Q_{σ(i)σ(j)}=p_ij. Honesty means, for every P and full internal state before a match, winning never gives a participant smaller conditional tournament-win probability than losing. P is doubly monotone if entries are nonincreasing down columns and nondecreasing along rows.

Origin: Strongest-player subquestion after (4.14). The equivalent weakest-player formulation is not counted separately.

For strictly decreasing nonnegative integer lists m=(m₁,…,mᵣ),n=(n₁,…,nₛ), put fₖ,±ᵗ(x)=e^{−x²/2}x^{1/2±t}Lₖ^{±t}(x²), where Lₖᵃ(y)=Σⱼ₌₀ᵏ(−1)ʲ binom(k+a,k−j)yʲ/j!. results.label: 2026-10-09: proposed counterexample
results.scope: The full face lattice of a convex 13-gon, including the empty and full faces, has Ehrhart linear coefficient -298495711/35302608. This is the only negative coefficient of its degree-28 Ehrhart polynomial; every coefficient is positive for polygon sizes 3 through 12. Limits: This disproves the Ehrhart coefficient question, distinct from the source's earlier negative order-polynomial coefficient for a 7-gon. Two separate exact arithmetic derivations verify the counterexample; no claim about other poset families is made.

ledger.title: Collection question 3617: Realizability of strongly Koszul masks
ledger.note: No. On n = 3 the mask with M(∅,k) = ∅; M({1},2) = {1,2}, M({1},3) = {1,3}; M({2},1) = M({3},1) = {2,3}, M({2},3) = {1,2}, M({3},2) = {1,3}; and M(A,k) = [3] for |A| = 2 satisfies every listed condition, with F_∅ = (1+z)²/(1−z). No algebra realizes it over any field: the forced Hilbert series leaves a two-dimensional space of quadric relations, the colon conditions remove x² from all of them, and M({2,3},1) = [3] needs x² ∈ (y,z). The catalog wording matches Definition 2.13 and Question 2.16 of the source; its follow-up (which properties to add) is not addressed. Reconstructed checkpoint without its original checkers; re-derived here by hand and spot-checked with independent exact computations on 10 October 2026. Not external peer review or a novelty certification. Filed from the public-repo research round seven-problems-2026-10-10.

title: Are cyclic arithmetic and Peano arithmetic exponentially separated in shortest proof size?…
text: Are cyclic arithmetic and Peano arithmetic exponentially separated in shortest proof size? Precisely, do ε>0 and arbitrarily large cyclic proofs π of sentences φ exist such that every PA proof of φ has size ≥2^{|π|^ε}? Use the ordinary sequent calculi with cut and symbol-count size. Cyclic arithmetic replaces induction by finite directed proof graphs over Robinson arithmetic; every infinite unfolded branch must admit, on some tail, a term trace respecting substitutions, nonincreasing at each step and strictly decreasing infinitely often through antecedent inequalities.

ledger.note: Yes for every integer genus h ≥ 1. ledger.title: Collection question 3778: Determine the computational complexity of computing the number of connected partitions of an…
ledger.note: Exact counting is #P-complete under polynomial-time Turing reductions, already for connected bipartite simple graphs. Subdivisions satisfy C(G^(ℓ)) = P_G(2^ℓ−ℓ−1, 2^ℓ−1) for a two-variable polynomial whose value at (1,0) counts connected spanning edge subsets, a #P-hard Tutte evaluation (Jaeger–Vertigan–Welsh); polynomially many even subdivisions recover it by interpolation. Limits: no parsimonious reduction; approximate counting and sampling are not addressed. Reconstructed checkpoint without its original checkers; re-derived here by hand and spot-checked with independent exact computations on 10 October 2026. Not external peer review or a novelty certification. Filed from the public-repo research round seven-problems-2026-10-10.

context:
Field: model theory/topological semigroups.

For countable relational A, End(A) comprises relation-preserving self-maps. Pointwise topology is inherited from A^A with A discrete. Semigroup topologies make composition jointly continuous; Polish means separable and completely metrizable. Here ω-categorical means Aut(A) has finitely many orbits on A^n for every n.

Spaces are real and Hausdorff. Fréchet locally convex spaces are complete and metrizable. Asplund means that each continuous convex real function on a nonempty open convex domain is Fréchet differentiable on a dense Gδ set. Here differentiability at x means a continuous linear ℓ exists with [f(x+th)−f(x)]/t→ℓ(h), uniformly for h in each bounded set. A quojection is a countable projective limit of Banach spaces with all canonical projections surjective.

Setup: Use French semistandard tableaux: rows weakly increase rightward and columns strictly increase upward. Fix partition weight λ, with ℓ positive parts. A composition α of ℓ, allowing zero parts, accepts T when applying these operations successively with its parts is permitted and ends empty.

source.author: Heng Ma
source.title: The height of discrete-time critical beta-splitting trees

context:
Paper-origin: Heng Ma, The height of discrete-time critical beta-splitting trees, arXiv:2609.14329v2, revised 16 September 2026; Open Problem 1.2, p.6. No doctoral origin is claimed.

Construct a rooted binary tree T_n recursively: each clade of m≥2 leaves independently splits into ordered sizes i,m−i with probability m/[2H_{m−1}i(m−i)], 1≤i<m, where H_j=Σ_{k=1}^j1/k; singletons stop. Let L_n be the maximum root-to-leaf edge count. Using natural logarithms, put C=min_{θ>1} θ/[2(ψ(θ)+γ)], where ψ=Γ′/Γ and γ is Euler’s constant.

The Gaussian refinement and competing smaller correction scales are not counted separately.

Source URL: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.14329v2 https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.18320v1 https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.14325v2 https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.24973v1

Setup: Input is an undirected graph with unit edge capacities and k specified source–sink pairs. Select as many pairs as possible and route one unit of flow for each selected pair. Setup: Input consists of n pairwise distinct positive integers f₁,…,f_n, encoded in binary. A feasible assignment pairs each frequency f_i with a distinct position b_i∈{1,…,n} and a distinct position c_i∈{n+1,…,2n}, using every position exactly once, such that c_i−b_i≥f_i. This is the paper’s explicit numerical-matching definition of 2-Visits Covering: each task is performed twice, with a minimum recovery gap rather than a maximum deadline gap.

Source URL: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28574v4
status_notes: Status: Conjecture 2 names this Definition 3 problem. The paper’s finite-window Definition 2 has a boundary discrepancy; its claimed equivalence is not used here. No later matching resolution found through 10 October 2026; no doctoral attribution is claimed.

Setup: Alice receives x∈{0,1}^n and Bob receives y∈{0,1}^n; they must decide whether some coordinate has x_i=y_i=1. First they exchange at most c classical bits using deterministic classical computation. Then they exchange at most q qubits using quantum computation. Arbitrary prior entanglement is allowed but cannot be accessed during the classical phase. Communication is interactive in each phase; the worst-case error is at most 1/10 on every input. Let q(n,c) be the least such quantum communication cost.

source.title: New Complexity Classes in Locally Checkable Labeling for Local Computation Algorithms

context:
Field: Local computation. Paper-origin; no doctoral attribution asserted.

Consider solvable LCLs on finite graphs of fixed bounded degree, with fixed finite input/output alphabets and fixed-radius validity rules. Vertices have polynomial-range unique identifiers and ordered ports; algorithms know n. A graph-oracle probe returns a vertex’s input label, adjacency list and ports. A stateless randomized LCA may probe any identifier and uses a random tape shared across queries. VOLUME instead must grow the probed region connectedly from the queried vertex, and sees only independent random strings attached to probed vertices, consistently shared across queries. Each algorithm’s simultaneously induced labeling must be valid with probability ≥1−1/n. Complexity is maximum probes for one vertex query.

source.title: Graphs with Independent Exact r-Covers for All r

context:
Field: Extremal graph theory. Genealogy led to Chau’s earlier paper Graphs with Independent Exact r-Covers for All r, arXiv:2501.05854v2 (8 April 2025); the thesis full text was unavailable.

For a finite simple d-regular graph G, an independent exact r-cover is an independent vertex set S such that every vertex outside S has exactly r neighbors in S. Let N(d) be the minimum number of vertices of a nonempty such graph having, for every integer 1≤r≤d, an independent exact r-cover; the covers may differ with r.

Origin: Robert Johnson’s 2024 question, recorded as Question 4.1; the surviving finite case is identified before Proposition 4.8, and the asymptotic question in Remark 4.9. Existence for every d is proved; known bounds give (2−o(1))d≤log N(d)≤d(log(4d)−1+o(1)); log is natural.

title: For integers n,k,b≥2, must every linearizable, nondeterministic solo-terminating n-process…
text: For integers n,k,b≥2, must every linearizable, nondeterministic solo-terminating n-process implementation of a scannable object with k fully reusable b-state components use at least k+ceil(n/(b−1)) b-state base objects?
subject: Theory of Computation & Algorithms

source.author: Sean Garnet Ovens
source.title: The Space Complexity of Asynchronous Algorithms from Bounded Size Base Objects

context:
Field: Distributed computing. Thesis conjecture, printed page 72.

A scannable object has k components, each supporting a read of its full state: Apply(i,op) invokes a component operation; Scan returns their entire state vector atomically. A component is fully reusable if every state can reach every other by operations. All n processes may apply and scan. Base objects are atomic deterministic state machines; their domain sizes count their complete states, including auxiliary information.

Here solo-termination means that from every reachable configuration, each process with an unfinished operation has some finite solo execution completing it. Linearizability requires operations to behave as an atomic sequential execution respecting real-time precedence.

title: Can a symmetric numerical semigroup fail to be representable?
label: Question 5.2.1
text: Can a symmetric numerical semigroup fail to be representable?
subject: Algebraic Geometry

source.author: Zsolt Baja and Tamás László
source.title: Flat semigroups and weighted homogeneous surface singularities

context:
Source URL: https://doi.org/10.2140/agt.2026.26.201

A numerical semigroup S is an additive submonoid of the nonnegative integers with finite complement. For S≠N, let F be its largest gap; S is symmetric if, for every integer n, n∈S exactly when F−n∉S. Call S representable if S={ℓ≥0:A_ℓ≠0} for the coordinate ring A, graded by a good effective C* action, of a complex normal weighted-homogeneous surface singularity whose link is a rational homology sphere.

Source URL: https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.03406 https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.13619
status_notes: Status: Paper-origin question. Checked arXiv:2511.03406v1, which studies already representable semigroups, and arXiv:2607.13619v1, which proves representability for finite intersections of proportionally modular semigroups. Neither settles all symmetric semigroups. No matching resolution found in the documented 10 October 2026 search.

source.title: Finite basis problem for involution semigroups of order four

context:
Source URL: https://doi.org/10.2140/pjm.2026.342.163

An involution semigroup is an associative semigroup S equipped with a unary operation * satisfying (x*)*=x and (xy)*=y*x*. It is finitely based if all identities valid in the signature (multiplication,*) follow from a finite set of such identities.

source.title: Baire-Type Properties of Topological Vector Spaces

context:
Source URL: https://doi.org/10.1007/s00025-026-02731-3

In a topological vector space E, (x_n) is Mackey null if a_n x_n→0 for some increasing unbounded sequence of positive real numbers a_n. Property (MK) means every Mackey-null sequence has this property: each subsequence contains a further subsequence whose series converges in E. A Tychonoff space is κ-Fréchet–Urysohn if each point in the closure of an open set U is a limit of a sequence in U. Baire means every countable intersection of open dense sets is dense. Write C_k(X) for continuous real-valued functions with compact-open topology.

Vertices are isotopy classes of pants decompositions; an edge replaces one curve within a one-holed torus or four-holed sphere by a curve intersecting it minimally, once or twice respectively. Edges have length one.

Let f∈C^{1,γ}_loc([0,∞)), 0<γ<1, satisfy f(0)=f(θ)=f(1)=0 for some θ∈(0,1), f′(0)<0, f′(θ)>0, f′(1)<0, f<0 on (0,θ)∪(1,∞), f>0 on (θ,1), and ∫_0^1f>0. Assume −ΔU=f(U) has a positive radial exponentially decaying solution on R^d with ker(−Δ−f′(U))∩L∞=span{∂_1U,…,∂_dU}.

For bounded positive classical solutions of −Δu=f(u) in Ω, u=0 on ∂Ω, define λ_u=sup{λ:∃ψ∈W^{2,d}_loc(Ω), ψ>0, (Δ+f′(u)+λ)ψ≤0}.
status_notes: Status: Paper-origin closing conjecture, retaining the combined hypotheses of Theorem1.5 and Proposition4.6. source.title: Random walk in a regenerating random environment

context: Fix a probability law ν on [0,1]. Start X_0=0 and sample iid right-jump probabilities (ω_x)_{x∈Z} with law ν. At each step, the walk jumps right from x with probability ω_x and left otherwise. After each step, independently with probability p, replace the entire environment by a fresh iid sample, independent of the past. For p∈[0,1], write v(p)=lim_{m→∞}X_m/m for the deterministic almost-sure speed; p=0 is the static model.
status_notes: Status: Paper-origin. title: Is derivability decidable in its fragment whose formulas are built only from propositional…
text: Is derivability decidable in its fragment whose formulas are built only from propositional variables, the left implication →, and !^s?
location: Thesis §6.2.1, page 70; earlier IJCAR 2022 paper by Blaisdell, Max Kanovich, Stepan L. Kuznetsov, Elaine Pimentel and Scedrov, §§3–4.
subject: Logic, Foundations & Set Theory

source.author: Eben Blaisdell
source.title: Subexponentials in Nonassociative Lambek Calculus

context:
Field: Mathematical logic and categorial grammar. Thesis §6.2.1, page 70; earlier IJCAR 2022 paper by Blaisdell, Max Kanovich, Stepan L. Kuznetsov, Elaine Pimentel and Scedrov, §§3–4.

Take the intuitionistic calculus acLL_Σ of that paper, with exactly one label s and f(s)={C,W,E,A1,A2}. Antecedents are ordered binary trees, with empty subtrees erased. Sequents have one succedent formula; no global structural rules apply. The modality !^s has dereliction and promotion, and licenses weakening, nonlocal contraction, exchange and both specified associativity rules, exactly as in Figures 1–2; contraction can identify separated copies of an entirely !^s-marked subtree.

Degree award was not independently established.

Origin: The dissertation restates the joint paper’s minimal-fragment question. No resolution found through 10 October 2026. Undecidability with additives, or with a second associativity-only modality, does not settle this fragment. The 2026 Galatos–Sangalli deducibility result also uses additive join.

source.title: Sampling Unlabeled Chordal Graphs in Expected Polynomial Time

context:
Field: Random graph generation. Restated in Hébert-Johnson’s dissertation §5.2; doctoral details appear above.

A chordal graph is a finite simple graph with no induced cycle of length at least four. Let U_n be its n-vertex isomorphism classes. An unlabeled sampler outputs a representative, with every class receiving probability 1/|U_n|, rather than assigning equal probability to all labeled graphs. Let T_n be its running time and X_n its output class.

Source URL: https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.STACS.2025.46

Field: Extremal graph enumeration. Doctoral context: Verónica Andrea Moyano, Problemas de dominación de aristas: algoritmos, cotas y propiedades (Universidad de Buenos Aires, doctorate in mathematics, 2017; adviser Min Chih Lin).

For a finite simple graph G, a perfect edge dominating set is F⊆E(G) such that every edge outside F shares an endpoint with exactly one edge of F. No analogous restriction is imposed on edges inside F. Let μ̃(G) count all such subsets, including E(G), rather than only minimum or inclusion-minimal ones. Let C_n denote the n-vertex cycle.

source.author: Eric Demer and Peter Selinger
source.title: On 3-terminal positions in Hex

context:
Field: Combinatorial game theory. Paper restatement of Selinger’s 2022 question; reached through the Bian–Selinger doctoral route.

Let P={⊥,a,b,c,⊤}, with a,b,c incomparable between bottom and top. Finite game forms are atoms [p], p∈P, or {L|R} with nonempty finite sets of earlier forms. Write Gᴸ,Gᴿ for options. Recursively, G≤H means every Gᴸ◁H, every G◁Hᴿ, and additionally G◁H if either game is atomic. Define G◁H when some Gᴿ≤H, some G≤Hᴸ, or both are atoms [p],[q] with p≤q. Equivalence means G≤H≤G. A form is passable when every follower F, including itself, satisfies F◁F.

A three-terminal Hex region is a finite set of hexagonal cells completely surrounded by stones, with three black and three white boundary components. Players fill empty hexagonal cells with their own colours. Its terminal atoms record black connectivity: ⊥ no pair, a only 2–3, b only 1–3, c only 1–2, ⊤ all three. Black moves are left options; white moves are right options.

Definition source: Selinger, Integers 22 (2022), #G3, Definitions 4.1, 4.3, 6.2.

Source URL: https://math.colgate.edu/~integers/wg3/wg3.pdf

Source URL: https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.08247
status_notes: Status: No later version, resolution or matching claim found through 10 October 2026.

source.author: Nacim Oijid
source.title: Complexity of Positional Games on Graphs

context:
Field: Positional games. Gledel–Oijid–Tavenas–Thomassé, On the Complexity of Client-Waiter and Waiter-Client Games, ICALP 2025, §6.

On an explicitly listed finite hypergraph, Waiter offers two unclaimed vertices; Client claims one and Waiter receives the other. An unpaired final vertex goes to Client. In Client-Waiter, Client wins by owning an entire hyperedge; otherwise Waiter wins.

In Waiter-Client, instead Waiter wins by owning an entire hyperedge. For a Waiter-winning hypergraph H let t(H) be the least number of offers within which Waiter can force victory. Let os(k) be the maximum t(H) among such H with maximum hyperedge size k.

Origin: Q4016 is thesis Conjecture 2.22, p.60; the final paper’s equivalent Tadpole problem remains open. Q4017 is paper Problem 1, p.89:16.

Maker-Maker domination: thesis pp.102,133, restating joint work with Duchêne, Dumas, Parreau and Rémila. A cograph has no induced four-vertex path. Two players alternately claim unclaimed vertices, starting with none claimed. The first whose own set dominates the finite simple graph wins; otherwise exhaustion is a draw. A set dominates when every vertex belongs to it or has a neighbour in it.

Source URL: https://nacim-oijid.fr/PhD_thesis_Nacim_Oijid.pdf

Source URL: https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.ICALP.2025.89

Source URL: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.dam.2024.01.023
status_notes: Status: No later resolution found through 10 October 2026. The thesis retains Q4018 after the May 2024 journal publication.

source.author: Mathieu Hilaire, Perig Montfort and Nacim Oijid
source.title: On the Complexity of the Maker-Breaker Happy Vertex Game

context:
Field: Algorithmic game theory. Paper-origin.

On a finite simple graph G, Maker and Breaker alternately colour one uncoloured vertex red and blue, respectively. The input specifies who starts. At exhaustion, Maker’s score counts vertices v whose closed neighbourhood N[v] is entirely red. Maker maximizes this score; Breaker minimizes it. Given an integer s, ask whether Maker can guarantee score at least s.

Neighborhood diversity w is the smallest number of vertex classes having identical neighbours outside their class, each class a clique or independent set.

Source URL: https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.FUN.2026.24

source.title: Token Positional Games

context:
Field: Positional games. Paper-origin.

A finite hypergraph H is explicitly listed. Maker has a red tokens and Breaker b blue tokens, initially off-board. Starting with Maker, players alternate placing an unused token on an empty vertex, moving an existing own token to any empty vertex, or passing. Vacated vertices become empty. Maker wins upon covering a hyperedge with red tokens; Breaker wins by preventing this indefinitely, including repetition of a state with the same player to move. This is the token-jumping (a,b)-game.

Source URL: https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.FUN.2026.5
status_notes: Status: The final published 15 May 2026 leaves these questions open; the EXPTIME-completeness result there concerns token sliding from preoccupied positions. No later resolution found through 10 October 2026.

Modular width w is the least w allowing G to be built from singletons by disjoint unions, complete joins and substitutions into templates of at most w vertices. Substitution replaces template vertices by graphs, adding all cross-edges exactly along template edges.

title: Is group isomorphism on finitely generated bi-orderable groups universal?

subject: Logic, Foundations & Set Theory

source.author: Filippo Calderoni and Adam Clay
source.title: The isomorphism problem for finitely generated bi-orderable groups
source.field: Group theory and descriptive set theory

context:
Represent finitely generated groups by normal subgroups N of the countably generated free group F∞ containing all but finitely many basis elements, with the inherited Borel structure from 2^{F∞}. Restrict to the indicated quotient groups F∞/N. Left/bi-orderability means existence of a total order invariant under left/both-sided multiplication. Amenability means existence of a left-invariant mean on bounded real functions.

A countable Borel equivalence relation E is universal if every countable Borel equivalence relation F admits a Borel map f with xFy⇔f(x)Ef(y). Weak universality instead requires a countable-to-one Borel map with xFy⇒f(x)Ef(y).

source.title: Ordered Groups, Computability and Cantor-Bendixson Rank

context:
Field: Computability and ordered groups.

A computable group has computable domain and multiplication; a computable copy is an isomorphic computable group. A bi-order is a two-sided invariant total order; computable orders have decidable comparison. Put X(G)={positive cones of bi-orders}, topologized inside {0,1}^G. Its Cantor–Bendixson rank is the first stage at which iteratively deleting isolated points stabilizes; limit stages take intersections. A computable ordinal has a computable well-order presentation.

source.author: Román Aranda, Sarah Blackwell, Geunyoung Kim, Patrick Naylor and Puttipong Pongtanapaisan
source.title: Bridge position of 3-manifolds embedded in the 5-sphere

context:
Field: Geometric topology.

A 3-knot is a smooth embedding S³⊂S⁵. Use the standard genus-zero quadrisection of S⁵ into four 5-balls. A bridge quadrisection meets every intersection of one, two or three sectors in boundary-parallel 3-disks, 2-disks or arcs, respectively; all four meet in 2b points on a 2-sphere. Its 4-plane diagram consists of planar diagrams of the four arc systems, sharing endpoints. Each pair closes to an unlink; each triple, capped by trivial disk systems, represents an unlink of 2-spheres. The crossing number minimizes the total crossings over such diagrams representing the knot.

Source URL: https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.12182
status_notes: Status checked 10 October 2026: no resolution found. The source proves that crossingless diagrams represent unknotted embeddings.

title: Are abelian surfaces X,Y derived isogenous exactly when there exists a quasiliftable principal…

subject: Algebraic Geometry

source.author: Zhiyuan Li and Haitao Zou
source.title: Derived isogenies and isogenies for abelian surfaces

context:
Field: Algebraic geometry.

Work over algebraically closed k of characteristic p>3. Within abelian surfaces, or within K3 surfaces, “derived isogenous” means connected by a finite chain of k-linear equivalences between bounded derived categories of Brauer-twisted coherent sheaves; consecutive equivalences may use different Brauer classes on their shared surface. An isogeny is a surjective homomorphism with finite kernel; principal means square degree. Quasiliftable means a finite composition of isogenies liftable to characteristic zero. Liftable means occurring as a special fiber over a mixed-characteristic discrete valuation ring. Km(X) is the minimal resolution of X/{±1}. Put W=W(k), the Witt-vector ring, and K₀=Frac(W). A derived isogeny is prime-to-p when each link’s even crystalline realization over K₀ maps the integral H^even_crys(−/W) lattices isomorphically.

Source URL: https://doi.org/10.2140/ant.2026.20.1185
status_notes: Status checked 10 October 2026: no matching resolution found. Known individual-equivalence and prime-to-p-isogeny results leave these residuals.

Let G,H be connected simply-connected solvable real Lie groups such that every adjoint operator ad(X) on either Lie algebra has real eigenvalues. Equip them with left-invariant Riemannian metrics. source.author: Ivan O. Shevchenko, Jun Liu and Xinzhi Liu
source.title: Global asymptotic stability of homogeneous polynomial vector fields is undecidable

context: Consider x′=F(x) on Rⁿ, n≥1, where F has rational coefficients and every monomial has degree d. The origin is Lyapunov stable if for every ε>0 some δ>0 makes all solutions starting within δ exist for t≥0 and remain within ε. Global asymptotic stability (GAS) additionally requires every solution to exist forward forever and tend to zero. Decision algorithms take finite rational coefficient lists.
status_notes: Status: Paper-origin residual questions. The source reports cubic undecidability in sufficiently large fixed dimensions; it leaves these thresholds and the quadratic decision problem unresolved. No matching resolution found on 10 October 2026.

source.author: Pieter Belmans, Sergey Galkin and Swarnava Mukhopadhyay
source.title: Can one hear the shape of a lattice random walk?

context: Let μ and ν be finitely supported probability laws on Zᵈ, d≥1, with μ(v)=μ(−v), ν(v)=ν(−v), and supports spanning Rᵈ. Their walks start at zero and have independent identically distributed increments with the respective laws. Define their shapes as conv(supp μ) and conv(supp ν); shapes agree when an invertible real linear map carries one onto the other.
status_notes: Status: Paper-origin. Symmetry forces zero mean, and spanning makes zero interior to each shape. Lattice-preserving equivalence and reconstruction of the step probabilities are not requested. The source’s nonsymmetric counterexamples and its equal-shape symmetric examples leave this question open. No matching resolution found on 10 October 2026.

subject: Topology

source.author: Surena Hozoori
source.title: Contact Geometric Theory of Anosov Flows in Dimension Three and Related Topics

context:
On a closed connected oriented smooth three-manifold M, a bi-contact structure is an everywhere-transverse pair ξ₋=kerα₋, ξ₊=kerα₊ of C¹ plane fields, where α₋∧dα₋<0 and α₊∧dα₊>0. Two contact structures are isotopic if an ambient isotopy carries one to the other; bi-contact homotopy is a continuous path of such transverse pairs. A contact structure is overtwisted if an embedded disk is tangent to its planes along its boundary, and tight otherwise.

In Rᵏ, k≥2, it has form {x:πₑx∈C₋, β(πₑx)<xₑ<τ(πₑx)}, where πₑ deletes one coordinate, C₋ is a recursive Λ-cell in Rᵏ⁻¹, and β,τ:Rᵏ⁻¹→R are globally Λ-Lipschitz for the norm ||y||∞=maxᵢ|yᵢ|, with β<τ on C₋. Let G=(V,E) be a countably infinite connected simple undirected graph of maximum degree Δ<∞. Assume two independent continuous-time random walks, each jumping at rate 1 to each neighbor and started together at any vertex, have almost surely finitely many collision entrances {t:Xₜ₋≠Yₜ₋, Xₜ=Yₜ}. Let α:V→(0,1) satisfy α(x)=Σᵧ∼ₓα(y)/deg(x).

For a finite nonzero nonnegative measure Λ on [0,1], the Λ-broadcast voter process has opinions in {0,1}. Each nonempty subset A of x's neighbors simultaneously adopts x's opinion at rate ∫q^(|A|−1)(1−q)^(deg(x)−|A|)Λ(dq), with endpoint values given by the polynomial. Write μₐ,Λ for its limiting distribution from independent Bernoulli(α(x)) opinions.

title: For every Banach B, is every generalized-hyperbolic f∈D(B) stable?
text: For every Banach B, is every generalized-hyperbolic f∈D(B) stable?
subject: Differential Equations & Dynamical Systems

source.author: Sergey Tikhomirov
source.title: Discontinuous Generalized Hyperbolicity and Structural Stability

context:
For a Banach space B, let D(B) consist of C¹-diffeomorphisms f:B→B with globally bounded Df,D(f⁻¹) and uniformly continuous Df. Set d₁(f,g)=supₓ||f(x)−g(x)||+supₓ||Df(x)−Dg(x)||.

Call f stable if ∀ε>0 ∃δ>0 ∀g∈D(B) with d₁(f,g)<δ, there is a homeomorphism H satisfying gH=Hf and max(||H−id||∞,||H⁻¹−id||∞)<ε.

Call f generalized-hyperbolic if ∃C>0, λ∈(0,1) and bounded linear projections Pₓ,Qₓ with Pₓ+Qₓ=id, B=Eₓˢ⊕Eₓᵘ, Eₓˢ=ran(Pₓ), Eₓᵘ=ran(Qₓ), ||Pₓ||,||Qₓ||≤C; Df(x)Eₓˢ⊆E_f(x)ˢ and D(f⁻¹)(x)Eₓᵘ⊆E_f⁻¹(x)ᵘ; and for every integer n≥1, ||Dfⁿ(x)|Eₓˢ||,||D(f⁻ⁿ)(x)|Eₓᵘ||≤Cλⁿ. These conditions hold for every x∈B; derivative and projection norms are operator norms. No regularity of x↦Pₓ,Qₓ is assumed.
status_notes: Status: Paper-origin. Q4101 already appears as Conjecture 13, p.8, in his Generalized hyperbolicity for diffeomorphisms of Banach spaces, arXiv:2510.05499v3. https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.05499v3 The 2026 source explicitly asks both directions. Linear shadowing results do not settle these nonlinear questions. No matching resolution found, 10 October 2026.

title: Does every locally compact quantum group admit an amenable action on some injective von Neumann…
text: Does every locally compact quantum group admit an amenable action on some injective von Neumann algebra?
subject: Functional Analysis & Operator Theory

source.author: Joeri Ludo De Ro
source.title: Equivariant W*-correspondences

context:
For a locally compact quantum group G, write M=L∞(G), with comultiplication Δ. An action is an injective normal unital *-homomorphism α:A→A⊗̄M satisfying (α⊗id)α=(id⊗Δ)α. It is amenable if there is a unital completely positive E:A⊗̄M→A with Eα=id and αE=(E⊗id)(id⊗Δ); E need not be normal. Injective means A admits a unital completely positive projection from B(K) in a faithful normal representation.

Vaes-closed means there is an injective normal unital *-homomorphism L∞(Ĥ)→L∞(Ĝ) intertwining comultiplications. Writing Δ_G,H:M→M⊗̄L∞(H) for its right coaction, restriction satisfies (α⊗id)α_H=(id⊗Δ_G,H)α.
status_notes: Status: The first question is thesis-recorded. The second appears already in De Ro, arXiv:2312.10738v2, Remark 8.3 (2024); accepted v3 retains it. No matching resolution found, 10 October 2026.

title: If X and X* are both Grothendieck, must X be reflexive?
text: If X and X* are both Grothendieck, must X be reflexive?
location: Problems 6, 7 and 28, pp. 16, 40; published Japanese Journal of Mathematics 16 (2021), 247–313.
subject: Functional Analysis & Operator Theory

source.author: Manuel González and Tomasz Kania
source.title: Grothendieck spaces: the landscape and perspectives

context: A real or complex Banach space X is Grothendieck if every sequence in its continuous dual X* converging in σ(X*,X) also converges in σ(X*,X**). Reflexive means that the canonical embedding X→X** is onto. Super-reflexive means admitting an equivalent uniformly convex norm. B(E) denotes all bounded linear operators E→E, with operator norm.
status_notes: Status: The first two restate Diestel’s 1973 Problems 6 and 4. The third is the super-reflexive operator-space question, also recorded in Kania’s 2019 Svratka lecture. These are paper-recorded questions, without doctoral attribution. No matching resolution found, 10 October 2026; the recent claim concerning ℓ∞(E) addresses a different space.

title: If Λ₁₁>1 and Λ₂₂>1, must uQ(u)=0 have a probability solution with u₀₀<1, for every γ≥0?
text: If Λ₁₁>1 and Λ₂₂>1, must uQ(u)=0 have a probability solution with u₀₀<1, for every γ≥0?
subject: Probability & Stochastic Processes

source.author: Karima Belatreche, Lamia Belhadji and Nicolas Lanchier
source.title: The contact process with social clusters and asymptomatic states

context:
Fix integer N≥3 and nonnegative λ₁,λ₂,φ₁,φ₂,γ. On S={(i,j)∈Z≥0²:i+j≤N}, let u be a probability row vector and b(u)=Σ_(i,j)∈S(iλ₁+jλ₂)uᵢⱼ. Define the generator Q(u) by transitions (0,0)→(1,0) at rate b(u), (i,j)→(i+1,j) at rate iφ₁+jφ₂ when i+j<N, (i,j)→(i−1,j+1) at rate iγ, and recovery transitions (i,j)→(i−1,j), (i,j)→(i,j−1) at rates i,j. Omit transitions outside S; all other off-diagonal rates vanish. Diagonal entries make row sums zero. The mean-field equation is u′=uQ(u).

Put Λᵢⱼ=λᵢΣₖ₌₀ᴺ⁻¹φⱼᵏ.
status_notes: Status: Paper-origin conjecture. The source proves the N=2 case; its spatial-process results do not establish this mean-field assertion for general N. No matching resolution found, 10 October 2026.

source.author: Hitesh Kumar, Bojan Mohar, Seyed Ahmad Mojallal and Shivaramakrishna Pragada
source.title: Stability of maximal relative projection constants

context:
All spaces and operators are real. For a linear subspace Y⊆Rⁿ, equip Rⁿ and Y with the maximum norm, and set λ(Y,Rⁿ)=inf{||P||:P:Rⁿ→Y is linear and P|Y=idY}. For integers n≥r≥1, define λ(r,n)=sup{λ(Y,Rⁿ):dimY=r}, and λ(r)=supₙ≥ᵣλ(r,n).

Let nᵣ be the least integer n≥r for which λ(r,m)=λ(r) for every integer m≥n. The source proves that nᵣ exists and nᵣ≤2ʳr(r+1)/2.
status_notes: Status: Paper-origin quadratic-threshold residual. The earlier Basso question asked whether stabilization occurs at all; the displayed exponential bound settles that existence question but leaves the quadratic bound open. This is about required ambient dimension, not a stability estimate for individual near-extremal Banach spaces. No matching resolution found, 10 October 2026.

source.author: Valmir Krasniqi
source.title: On the Alzer–Berg problem: an optimal Bernstein boundary and a uniqueness conjecture

context:
A nonnegative smooth function h on (0,∞) is Bernstein if (−1)ⁿh⁽ⁿ⁺¹⁾≥0 for every integer n≥0. For 0<c<1, set Hₐ,c(y)=(1+1/y)^(ay−c) and A_c=sup{a>0:Hₐ,c is Bernstein}. The source proves 0<A_c<3−c.

For 0<a<3−c, define q₁=a/2+c, q₂=a/3+c/2+q₁²/2, wₐ,c(s)=π⁻¹[s/(1−s)]^(as+c)sin(π(as+c)), and

Dₐ,c(t)=q₁+(q₁−q₂)t+e^(−a)∫₀¹wₐ,c(s)[e^((1−s)t)−1−(1−s)t]ds.
status_notes: Status: This is the source’s combined uniqueness-and-quadratic-contact conjecture, with c=−b. The proved boundary theorem gives a finite nonempty set of positive zeros of even order, but neither uniqueness nor order two. The parameter-domain classification is already established and is not asked again. No matching resolution found, 10 October 2026.

title: Determine Cα for every irrational α.
label: Question 8.3
text: Determine Cα for every irrational α.
subject: Differential Equations & Dynamical Systems

source.author: Nicanor Carrasco-Vargas
source.title: Isomorphisms and slow entropy of deterministic [T,T⁻¹] systems

context:
Let T=R/Z with Lebesgue probability measure, Rα(θ)=θ+α modulo 1, and τ=1_[0,1/2)−1_[1/2,1). For irrational α, define Cα to be the set of pairs (c,ℓ)∈T×{−1,1} for which there is a measurable integer-valued function f:T→Z satisfying

τ(θ+c)−ℓτ(θ)=f(θ+α)−f(θ)

for almost every θ.
status_notes: Status: Paper-origin classification question. When α has bounded continued-fraction coefficients, the source records precisely (c,ℓ)=(kα,1) or (kα+1/2,−1), k∈Z. For other rotation numbers extra shifts can occur; the paper does not give the general classification. The transfer function is merely measurable, with no continuity, boundedness or integrability imposed. Known isomorphism-rigidity theorems for the skew products do not supply this missing arithmetic description. No matching resolution found, 10 October 2026.

title: Must every real dual Banach space with a unique isometric predual have a strongly unique…
text: Must every real dual Banach space with a unique isometric predual have a strongly unique isometric predual?
location: introduction, p.1; recorded in Godefroy’s 1989 survey, Problem (2), p.186
subject: Functional Analysis & Operator Theory

source.author: Ramón J. Aliaga, Marek Cúth and Felipe Vico
source.title: Lipschitz-free spaces are strongly unique preduals

context: Let X be a real dual Banach space. Say X has a unique isometric predual if any two real Banach spaces Y,Z whose continuous duals are linearly isometric to X are themselves linearly isometric. Say its isometric predual is strongly unique if, for every such Y,Z, every surjective linear isometry T:Y*→Z* is continuous from σ(Y*,Y) to σ(Z*,Z). Equivalently, each T is the adjoint of a surjective linear isometry Z→Y.
status_notes: Status: Recorded in Godefroy’s 1989 survey, Problem (2), p. 186, this question is restated as unresolved here; no doctoral attribution is made. The paper’s theorem concerns Lipschitz-free preduals, and does not settle the equivalence for arbitrary dual Banach spaces. Nonisometric predual categories are different questions. No matching resolution found, 10 October 2026.

source.author: Jinghao Huang, Fedor Sukochev and Dmitriy Zanin
source.title: Lack of isomorphic embedding from Lorentz function spaces into Lorentz operator ideals

context:
For p,q>0, let Cₚ,ᵩ consist of compact operators A on complex ℓ₂ whose nonincreasing singular values sₙ(A) satisfy

||A||ₚ,ᵩ=(Σₙ≥₁[n^(q/p)−(n−1)^(q/p)]sₙ(A)^q)^(1/q)<∞.

This is a quasi-norm. Lq(0,1) uses complex scalars and Lebesgue measure. An isomorphic embedding J:Lq(0,1)→Cₚ,ᵩ is a linear map with constants 0<a≤b<∞ such that a||f||q≤||Jf||ₚ,ᵩ≤b||f||q for all f.
status_notes: Status: Paper-recorded residual. The region 2<p≤q is already excluded. The new nonembedding theorem handles non-Lebesgue Lorentz domains but leaves this Lq case. The read manuscript explicitly says to appear in Advances in Mathematics; matching final metadata gives volume 504, article 111276, DOI 10.1016/j.aim.2026.111276. No substantive discrepancy or matching later resolution found, 10 October 2026.
