source.author: Geunsu Choi
source.title: A bi-Lipschitz characterization of strong minimum-attainment for Lipschitz maps

context: Let (M,d,0) be a complete pointed metric space with at least two points, and Y a real Banach space. Lip₀(M,Y) consists of Lipschitz maps f:M→Y with f(0)=0, under ||f||Lip=supₚ≠ᵩ||f(p)−f(q)||/d(p,q). Put m(f)=infₚ≠ᵩ||f(p)−f(q)||/d(p,q). Let SMA(M,Y) comprise those f for which this infimum is attained at two distinct points.
status_notes: Status: Paper-origin vector-valued classification. The scalar case is settled: density fails exactly when M is bi-Lipschitz equivalent to a positive-Lebesgue-measure subset of R. The paper gives counterexamples to directly extending that criterion to general Y, rather than a replacement classification. Norm-attainment and minimum-attainment are different approximation problems. No matching resolution found, 10 October 2026.

source.title: The Ball-Covering Property in Lipschitz-Free Spaces

context: All spaces are real; metric spaces M are complete and pointed. Lip₀(M) is the space of real Lipschitz functions vanishing at the basepoint, with Lipschitz-constant norm. F(M) is the closed linear span of evaluations δₓ in Lip₀(M)*. A Banach space has BCP if countably many open norm-balls, none containing zero, cover its unit sphere.

title: If X has WRNP in the stated curve sense, must X̂ have RNP?

subject: Functional Analysis & Operator Theory

source.author: Fernando Albiac, José L. Ansorena and Pietro Wald
source.title: Differentiability of Lipschitz curves in p-Banach spaces

context:
Let X be a real or complex quasi-Banach space with continuous quasi-norm. Here WRNP means: every Lipschitz F:[0,1]→X is weakly differentiable almost everywhere, with one exceptional null set, meaning that at each remaining t some v∈X satisfies (x*∘F)′(t)=x*(v) for every continuous linear functional x*∈X*.

Set pₑ(x)=inf{Σⱼ₌₁ᵐ||xⱼ||:m≥1, x=Σⱼ₌₁ᵐxⱼ}. The Banach envelope X̂ is the completion of X/ker(pₑ) under pₑ. A Banach space has RNP exactly when every Lipschitz curve into it is norm-differentiable almost everywhere.
status_notes: Status: Paper-origin question. The result is known for spaces with a boundedly complete Schauder basis. The paper’s counterexample has an RNP envelope but fails WRNP, addressing the reverse direction only. No point-separating dual is assumed. No matching resolution found, 10 October 2026.

source.author: Christian Cobollo, Romuald Ernst, Quentin Menet and Alfred Peris
source.title: Hypercyclicity and Lipschitz-free operators

context: Let (M,d,0) be a countable pointed metric space whose every point except possibly 0 is isolated, and let f:M→M be Lipschitz with f(0)=0. Define real Lip₀(M) using the Lipschitz-constant norm and F(M)=closure span{δₓ:x∈M}⊆Lip₀(M)*, where δₓ(g)=g(x). The bounded linear operator T_f:F(M)→F(M) is determined by T_fδₓ=δ_f(x). It is hypercyclic if some μ∈F(M) has norm-dense orbit {T_fⁿμ:n≥0}.
status_notes: Status: Paper-origin classification question. The targeting criterion is proved only under additional metric or basis assumptions, and the paper explicitly leaves the full countable isolated-nonzero setting unresolved. No completeness, uniform discreteness or Schauder-basis assumption is added to the stated problem. This is separate from whether hypercyclicity implies weak mixing. No matching resolution found, 10 October 2026.

title: Do such A,T exist for every x that is neither Schnorr random nor weakly 1-generic, with T…
text: Do such A,T exist for every x that is neither Schnorr random nor weakly 1-generic, with T additionally ergodic?
subject: Logic, Foundations & Set Theory

source.author: Joey Veltri
source.title: Effective recurrence for computable measure-preserving transformations

context:
On Cantor space 2^N use fair-coin measure λ. Effectively open means a computably enumerable union of cylinders; Π⁰₁ means effectively closed. A Schnorr test is a uniformly effectively open sequence (Uₙ) with uniformly computable measures λ(Uₙ)≤2^(−n); Schnorr-random points avoid every such intersection. Weakly 1-generic points belong to every dense effectively open set; 1-generic points avoid the boundary of every effectively open set. A total map T is computable if cylinder preimages are uniformly effectively open.

Seek a Π⁰₁ set A containing x with positive computable λ(A), and a total computable λ-preserving T:2^N→2^N with Tᵏ(x)∉A for every k≥1.
status_notes: Status: These are paper-origin questions. The larger point class in Q4133 and stronger dynamical requirement in Q4132 prevent either from being an immediate weaker formulation of the other. No matching resolution found, 10 October 2026.

title: Does a K₂-hypohamiltonian graph of girth at most four exist?
text: Does a K₂-hypohamiltonian graph of girth at most four exist?
subject: Combinatorics & Graph Theory

source.author: Jarne Renders
source.title: Studying Cycles with Computational Graph Theory
source.advisors: Jan Goedgebeur and Carol T. Zamfirescu

context:
Field: Structural graph theory. Thesis §8.1, p.175.

Graphs are finite, simple and connected. A Hamiltonian cycle visits every vertex exactly once. A graph is K₂-hypohamiltonian if it has no Hamiltonian cycle but deleting the endpoints of any edge leaves a graph with one. Girth is the length of a shortest cycle.

Origin: Older question, restated by Jan Goedgebeur, Jarne Renders, Gábor Wiener and Carol T. Zamfirescu in K₂-Hamiltonian Graphs: II; reaffirmed here. No matching resolution found through 10 October 2026. The high-girth and bipartite existence problems are different questions.

source.author: Jan Goedgebeur, Edita Máčajová and Jarne Renders
source.title: The Frank number and nowhere-zero flows on graphs

context:
Field: Graph orientations. Accepted manuscript arXiv:2305.02133v4, §1, Conjecture 1, p.2.

Graphs are finite, simple and 3-edge-connected. The Frank number fn(G) is the minimum number of orientations such that, for each edge e, deleting its oriented arc leaves a strongly connected digraph in at least one orientation. Strong connectivity requires directed paths between every ordered pair of vertices. Cyclic 4-edge-connectivity means deleting fewer than four edges cannot separate two components each containing a cycle.

source.author: Stijn Cambie, Jan Goedgebeur and Jorik Jooken
source.title: The maximum number of connected sets in regular graphs

context:
Field: Extremal graph enumeration. Final article, Conjecture 2, p.3; §6, p.17; definitions p.2.

For finite simple G, let N(G) count nonempty vertex sets inducing connected subgraphs and c(G)=N(G)^(1/|V(G)|). For integer d≥2, let c_d(n) maximize c(G) over d-regular n-vertex graphs, and c_d=limsup c_d(n) over orders admitting such graphs. A d-regular graph of girth g is Moore if its order equals 1+d∑_{i=0}^{r−1}(d−1)^i for g=2r+1, or 2∑_{i=0}^{r−1}(d−1)^i for g=2r.

Origin: Joint-paper conjecture and concluding question. No matching resolution or relevant erratum found through 10 October 2026.

source.title: On the order-diameter ratio of girth-diameter cages

context:
Field: Extremal graph theory. Journal PDF, also arXiv:2511.21144v3 (19 August 2026), §5, Question 1, p.16.

Graphs are finite, simple, undirected and connected. For integers k≥2, g≥3 and d≥1, a (k;g,d)-cage is a k-regular graph having girth exactly g and diameter exactly d, with the fewest vertices among graphs satisfying all three conditions, whenever any exist. Girth is shortest-cycle length; diameter is greatest vertex distance.

Origin: Joint-paper question, stronger than the classical even-girth cage conjecture. No later matching resolution found through 10 October 2026.

Field: Computational complexity. Final article, §7, Open Problem 1, p.67; definitions pp.59–60.

Graphs are finite, simple and undirected; the positive integer k is part of the input. Disjoint Paths asks, given k pairwise disjoint terminal pairs (s_i,t_i), with s_i≠t_i, for pairwise vertex-disjoint paths joining the prescribed pairs. Disjoint Connected Subgraphs instead receives pairwise disjoint terminal sets Z_i and asks for pairwise vertex-disjoint connected subgraphs containing the respective sets. H-free means no induced H; P_n is an n-vertex path; + denotes disjoint union.

Field: Computational complexity. Final article, §7, pp.2602–2603; definitions pp.2581–2582.

For finite simple undirected G and pairwise disjoint terminal sets Z₁,…,Z_k, Induced Disjoint Connected Subgraphs asks for vertex sets D_i⊇Z_i such that each G[D_i] is connected, the D_i are pairwise disjoint, and no edge joins distinct D_i. Field: Knot theory.

For a nontrivial smooth knot K⊂S³, let g_f(K) be the least genus of a Seifert surface with free fundamental group of its complement, and σ_t(V_K) the difference between the largest and smallest exponents of its Jones polynomial. Define td(K) as the minimum depth over ordinary oriented binary skein trees for all diagrams of K: each vertex branches by switching one crossing and by its oriented smoothing; leaves are unlinks. Depth is the maximum root-to-leaf edge count, counting both edge types; Reidemeister moves and diagram isotopies have zero cost.

context:
Field: Four-dimensional topology.

Here f:X→S² is relatively minimal, X is a closed connected smooth oriented 4-manifold, regular fibers are connected, critical values are distinct, and the nonempty critical locus consists only of positive Lefschetz singularities. Relative minimality excludes fiber spheres of self-intersection −1. A two-section is a possibly disconnected embedded oriented surface disjoint from Crit(f), restricting to a degree-two simple branched cover of S² with only positive branch points.

Source URL: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01776v1
